text.p: Portugal's biggest mobile phone operator Telecel, benefiting from a surge in demand for mobile phones, on Wednesday posted a sharp rise in 1996 profits to 7.3 billion escudos ($43 million), up from 2.4 billion in 1995.
Telecel president Antonio Carrapatoso said he expected that Telecel would pay good dividends for 1997.

"With the results of 1997 and our forecasts for investment, it should be possible, with the approval of shareholders, to issue good dividends for 1997," he told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
Telecel has issued no dividends so far. Some 40 percent of the company was floated last December.
Telecel expected to post a higher profit in 1997 than in 1996, Carrapatoso said.
"We are confident that if market conditions continue to be favourable, profits will be higher in 1997 than in 1996," he said. He gave no figures.
Telecel and its rival TMN, a unit of Portugal Telecom, control the Portuguese cellular phone market.

Carrapatoso said Telecel planned to reduce its prices in March in response to price cuts announced by TMN. He gave no details. TMN had said it would reduce prices on its products by up to 30 percent effective on March 1.
Carrapatoso said Telecel would hold investment levels steady in 1997, compared with 1996, while average revenue per customer would fall more than in recent years.
Average monthly revenues per client fell four percent to 17,233 escudos in 1996, compared with 1995, and should fall further in 1997 due to the impact of price cuts, he said.

"The average revenue per client will fall by more in 1997 than in recent years, especially because of the drop in prices and the greater weighting of families among our clients," Carrapatoso told a news conference.
Telecel said it spent 14.8 billion escudos on investment in 1996, 31 percent more than in 1995. ($1=168.995 escudos)
